content:
incident-bot: PAGED @eng-oncall - high tail latency and 5xx spike on recommender-service (prefetch path). auto-detect flagged cache eviction storm. pagerduty:sev2 :rotating_light:
anya: saw it. tail p99 for /v1/generate jumped to ~3.2s and error rate to 1.8% starting ~1923456700. reproducing on staging with load pattern similar to prod prefetch.
ryan: linking the graphs: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123/recommender?orgId=1
micah: looks like continuous-batcher started keeping much larger prefix keys in KV due to eviction policy change merged yesterday (PR #3657). prefetch started populating hot prefixes aggressively.
sara: can you paste the offending diff?
micah: sure - in config we set prefetch.max_items=5000 -> should have been 500. the intention was to increase throughput for cold-starts but it kept filling KV shards.
micah: patch snippet:
```yaml
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  max_items: 5000   # oops
  batch_window_ms: 20
```
anya: that explains cache amplification + longer iteration to evict -> batcher backs up -> CPU rises -> HPA scales up and down -> thrash. that causes tail latency.
ryan: confirmed HPA events show rapid scale ups starting 1923456720:
```
kubectl get hpa recommender-batcher -o yaml
metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      currentAverageUtilization: 85
      targetAverageUtilization: 60
```
micah: mitigation proposal: revert prefetch.max_items to 500, reduce batcher concurrency to 4, and bump HPA stabilizationWindow to 120s. also temporarily pin model-variant to lighter quantized model for recommender to drop CPU.
sara: +1 to revert. I'll prepare a rollback PR and run canary.
anya: asap steps im doing now: 1) add hotfix PR to set max_items=500 and batcher.concurrency=4 2) set HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds=120 and scaleDown/stabilization policy 3) gate canary to 10% traffic 4) flip model to q4_0 temporarily
devops-bot: started rolling restart for recommender-batcher pods (maxUnavailable=1).
anya: logs during spike, showing eviction churn:
```
2026-03-15T12:26:11Z WARN kv_shard.go:214 eviction: removed 12000 keys in 30s for shard-7
2026-03-15T12:26:12Z ERROR batcher.go:487 processing backlog=540 ms=3120 cpu=92%
```
ryan: customer-impact: CS reported increase in latency for two enterprise tenants using real-time recommendations, they saw 10-15% error spikes between 12:26-12:34 UTC. open ticket #CS-882.
customer-success: we've notified affected customers and offered to extend SLAs. they asked for root cause and ETA for stabilization.
micah: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/recommender/pull/3699 - describes change and includes unit/integration tests for prefetch guard.
anya: rolling out hotfix now to k8s-np (canary) -> applying configmap update and patching deployment.
devops-bot: canary applied to 2/20 pods: recommender-batcher-0, recommender-batcher-1. health checks passing.
anya: monitoring metrics, CPU dropping on canary pods to ~48% and p99 latency to ~420ms (down from 3.2s).
ryan: beginning broader rollout with 50% traffic shift. HPA stabilizationWindow applied.
micah: note: need follow-up to add e2e for prefetch upper bounds and telemetry to detect cache-occupancy growth before eviction storm.
sara: after rollout, note a small regression in throughput for a specific batch type - need to verify cost impact vs latency. create a ticket for Optimize team.
anya: handoff to @oncall-next in 20m. summary for next: root cause = mistaken prefetch.max_items increase, effects = KV eviction storm -> batching backlog -> CPU HPA thrash -> p99 latency and 5xx spike. immediate fix = rollback max_items, reduce batcher concurrency, HPA stabilizationWindow increase, temporary model pin. check grafana panels: batcher backlog, kv-occupancy, hpa-events, customer-errors.
oncall-next: noted. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hr and coordinate with CS on customer updates. will pick up postmortem draft and assign owners for follow-ups: micah (root cause + code guard), sara (throughput/cost analysis), ryan (HPA tuning + runbook update).
incident-bot: incident annotated as RESOLVED -> mitigation applied, monitoring OK for 10m. postmortem: draft required within 72h. :white_check_mark:
